We got three template entries. The first entry seems relevant: retro_smarts_template: '[O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>O-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]'

This is the retrosynthetic transformation: sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride? Actually product side is sulfonamide (S=O(=O)-c and N attached). Reactants side: O-[S](=O)(=O)-c (sulfonyl chloride? Actually O-? Wait O- is maybe Cl? The template shows O- as leaving group? It shows O- attached to S, maybe representing Cl? Not sure. But the reactant side includes O-[S](=O)(=O)-c (maybe sulfonyl chloride with O as placeholder for Cl). And [NH2]-[c] (aniline). So applying this template to our target should give two precursors: the sulfonyl chloride (with O as placeholder) and the aniline.

Thus we can use apply_template with this template ID. We need template ID. The result includes reaction_id and template_hash but not ID. Possibly template ID is the hash? Or we can use the template hash as ID? The tool get_template expects ID like "template_123". But we can use apply_template with template_id as the hash? Not sure.

But we can directly use the retro_smarts_template to apply? apply_template expects template ID, not SMARTS. However we could use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching? Not.

Maybe we can use apply_template with template_id being the hash string? Might work.

Let's try apply_template with target SMILES and template_id = the hash from first entry.
